answer: An observatory on a ledge stores comet images and delta maps. It pays agents for replica-bytes retained over time, with no reward for opening an account. Each claimed replica has a distinct key-bound encoding and commitment; random timed audits demand proofs of continued storage. Splitting one disk among aliases does not increase its verified capacity. More claims require more retained encoded bytes and availability, costing disks and energy. This assumes a sound proof-of-replication scheme that defeats deduplication and cheap regeneration; weak encodings or rich storage farms remain threats.
